answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by anchoring each identity to a licensed saffron plot on a tidal inlet marsh. The holder hand-picks stigmas in the two-week bloom, the yield weighed by an independent spice registrar, and a dried saffron sample sealed as a relic in that identity's vial. Random checks summon the holder to their own plot within a day, and one harvester cannot pick two plots in one bloom. The plot fee in outside money doubles per identity on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another real plot, another harvest season, another human, and twice the prior fee.
